testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: In an air tank
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve is located in the air tank that receives air first from the compressor.

questions.question: Friction inside a brake drum happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Each system has separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks, but each has its own separate hoses and lines.
Each system uses the same lines and hoses.
One system is the main braking system and a second system is ready if the first one fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may not work.
questions.explanation: If air pressure drops too low, the brakes will stop working. Pressing the brake pedal unnecessarily can let air out faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems operated by one set of controls. Each system operates the brakes on different axles.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks are used in an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: The number varies.
questions.explanation: The number and size of air storage tanks varies by vehicle. These tanks hold the compressed air for the braking system.

questions.question: Spring brakes turn on:

options.text: When too much air pressure is lost.
When a control on the dashboard is activated.
When the tires have minimal tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: When too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure drops to an unsafe level. You should exit the road safely and stop the vehicle as soon as you see the low pressure warning light.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has a single air brake system, but uses two sets of controls.
Has one air brake system for each side of the truck.
Has two brakes for each wheel.
Has two separate air brake systems, but uses a single set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems, but uses a single set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems that work with one set of brake controls. One system operates the brakes on the rear axle. The other system operates the brakes on the front axle.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: There is a decreased risk of jackknifing.
There is an increased risk of jackknifing.
The brakes will not work as effectively as they would without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a decreased risk of jackknifing.
questions.explanation: When the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, the risk of jackknifing is reduced. The driver can still maintain steering control. If only the trailer has ABS, it is less likely to swing out to one side.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes is ____ in one minute.
questions.correctAnswerText: 2 psi
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test on a single vehicle with air brakes, leakage should be no more than 2 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle should not be driven because it needs repairs.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: Newer vehicles have a yellow diamond-shaped knob to control the parking brake. Pull the knob out to engage the brake. Push it in to release the brake.

questions.question: Front brake limiting valves were designed to:

options.text: Stop the front tires from skidding.
Keep the front tires from overheating.
Use the front and rear brakes equally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older air brake vehicles have front brake limiting valves. They were meant to prevent front wheels from skidding. However, research showed these valves are not needed, so they should be left in the normal position.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:

options.text: Be very careful because the brakes might fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one system leaks:

options.text: The other system may not be affected.
There is nothing to worry about.
The other system will also leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other system may not be affected.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: To inspect slack adjusters on S-cam brakes, you must:

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes.
Put on gloves and push the slack adjusters.
Remove the drum and look inside.
Block the wheels and release the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block the wheels and release the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground. Place wheel blocks and release the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: To check if a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To see if a trailer has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires near the back of the brakes.

questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove water and oil that build up in the tanks. They can be manual or automatic.

questions.question: The most common foundation brake type is:
questions.correctAnswerText: S-cam drum brake.
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, the maximum air leak during a static leakage test is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle, the air brake system should not leak more than 3 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If it leaks faster, do not drive the vehicle—it needs repair.

questions.question: Front wheel braking works:
questions.correctAnswerText: In all road conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works in all road conditions. Front wheels rarely skid, even on ice.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of the air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes in an air brake system. Not all air brake vehicles have this gauge.

questions.question: If spring brakes are activated, what should you never do?

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Which is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: An axle brake system
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate braking systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens when air pressure is lost and spring brakes activate?

options.text: You will be unable to move the vehicle.
A separate air tank can be used to release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use the spring brakes to drive normally.
The air tanks will automatically refill to a safe pressure level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can be used to release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank. This tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Pushing the correct control will release the spring brakes for a short time, allowing you to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What are air tank drains used for?

options.text: To allow rainwater to enter the tank.
To drain water and compressor oil from the air tank.
They must remain open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: To drain water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil buildup. If not drained, damage can occur. Manually operated drains should be used at the end of each driving day.
